subject: [PATCH v2 00/11] nfsd: various delegated timestamp fixes

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about nfsd_break_deleg_cb() running multiple times per lease, which causes cl_delegs_in_recall to be incremented but not decremented correctly. The author explained that this is due to the function being called directly by dir notification paths and lm_break, and provided a fix to skip incrementing cl_delegs_in_recall when dl_recalled is already set.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern that NFSv4.0 clients can get write delegations when reclaiming a write open during the grace period, and agreed to apply the same check to CLAIM_PREVIOUS as is done for CLAIM_NULL and CLAIM_FH.
reviews.raw_body:
nfs4_open_delegation() refuses delegations for NFSv4.0 write opens on
CLAIM_NULL and CLAIM_FH, as its comment explains, but CLAIM_PREVIOUS
skips the check. An NFSv4.0 client reclaiming a write open during grace
can therefore get a write delegation, and NFSD can never complete a
GETATTR that the client sends before DELEGRETURN in the same compound.

Apply the same check to CLAIM_PREVIOUS.

Fixes: 1d3dd1d56ce8 ("NFSD: Enable write delegation support")
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c b/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c
index 5c2151b329c4..4b28553efc8d 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c
@@ -7533,6 +7533,9 @@ nfs4_open_delegation(struct svc_rqst *rqstp, struct nfsd4_open *open,
 	open->op_recall = false;
 	switch (open->op_claim_type) {
 		case NFS4_OPEN_CLAIM_PREVIOUS:
+			if (open->op_share_access & NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_WRITE &&
+			    clp->cl_minorversion == 0)
+				goto out_no_deleg;
 			if (!cb_up)
 				open->op_recall = true;
 			break;

-- 
2.56.1

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern that the ctime should be updated when a delegated atime update is sent along with other attribute changes. They added ATTR_CTIME to the iattr unless the request is a delegated atime-only update, ensuring that ctime is updated in such cases.
reviews.raw_body:
__nfsd_setattr() adds ATTR_CTIME only when ATTR_DELEG is clear, to keep
a delegated atime-only update from moving ctime. But ATTR_DELEG is set
for the whole iattr, so a holder's chmod or chown sent along with a
delegated atime changes the mode or owner without updating ctime.

Add ATTR_CTIME unless the request is a delegated atime-only update. A
delegated mtime whose ctime fails vetting now moves ctime to the current
time instead of leaving ctime alone.

Fixes: f9a348e0de19 ("nfsd: don't set the ctime on delegated atime updates")
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/vfs.c | 8 +++++---
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/vfs.c b/fs/nfsd/vfs.c
index 4a5674e583cc..7bc251d55c3c 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/vfs.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/vfs.c
@@ -513,10 +513,12 @@ static int __nfsd_setattr(struct dentry *dentry, struct iattr *iap)
 	/*
 	 * If ATTR_DELEG is set, then this is an update from a client that
 	 * holds a delegation. If this is an update for only the atime, the
-	 * ctime should not be changed. If the update contains the mtime
-	 * too, then ATTR_CTIME should already be set.
+	 * ctime should not be changed. Any other attribute change, such as
+	 * a mode or owner change sent along with a delegated atime, must
+	 * update the ctime.
 	 */
-	if (!(iap->ia_valid & ATTR_DELEG))
+	if (!(iap->ia_valid & ATTR_DELEG) ||
+	    (iap->ia_valid & ~(ATTR_DELEG | ATTR_ATIME | ATTR_ATIME_SET)))
 		iap->ia_valid |= ATTR_CTIME;
 
 	return notify_change(&nop_mnt_idmap, dentry, iap, NULL);

-- 
2.56.1

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the potential for a client to be destroyed while waiting for a GETATTR reply, which could lead to a freed nfs4_client being accessed by nfsd4_put_stid(). The author explained that taking a client reference along with the delegation reference under flc_lock prevents this issue. A new function, nfsd4_get_leased_deleg(), is introduced to take both references, and nfsd4_put_leased_deleg() drops them when done.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about missing freeze protection for filesystems in certain NFSv4 delegation update paths, explained that the issue is due to the lack of superblock's freeze protection being held while updating timestamps, and provided patches to add freeze protection checks and notifications when trying to update timestamps on frozen filesystems.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing LLM's review feedback on bugs in the existing delegated timestamp support code, which they are reworking. They confirm that their v2 patch series fixes these bugs and can be applied ahead of the ongoing work.
reviews.raw_body:
This version fixes up some bugs that Sashiko pointed out, as well as a
nit that Aurlien pointed out.

While I was reworking NFSD's delegated timestamp support, LLM review
found several bugs in the existing code. This series fixes them.

The timestamp rework is still a work in progress. These fixes can go in
ahead of it.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
Changes in v2:
- nfsd_setattr(): sanitize a fresh copy of the attributes under
  inode_lock on each attempt, since the setid bits a chown must clear
  depend on the current mode
- cb_getattr_update_times(): pin fi_deleg_file for the mount's write
  access, and skip the update once the delegation is unhashed
- nfsd4_deleg_set_times(): set dl_setattr only after notify_change()
  succeeds
- add the missing Signed-off-by to the nfsd_setattr() inode_lock patch
- reword changelogs and comments
- don't use ! operator on cl_minorversion
- Link to v1: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261120-delegts-fixes-v1-0-c89b37d2d462@kernel.org

---
Jeff Layton (11):
      nfsd: don't hold inode_lock while waiting for a delegation in nfsd_setattr()
      nfsd: take freeze protection before updating delegation timestamps
      nfsd: count a delegation in cl_delegs_in_recall only once
      nfsd: don't grant write delegations to NFSv4.0 clients on CLAIM_PREVIOUS
      nfsd: set ctime when a SETATTR with delegated times changes other attributes
      nfsd: pin the client while a GETATTR holds a conflicting delegation
      nfsd: recall when a CB_GETATTR reply omits the size
      nfsd: apply delegated times in a separate times-only setattr
      nfsd: grant a plain read delegation when timestamps are wanted on a read open
      nfsd: check fi_had_conflict under deleg_lock before hashing a delegation
      nfsd: take the write delegation grant stat before hashing

 fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c     | 171 ++++++++++++++++++++----------
 fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c    | 281 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-----------

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the correctness of delegating atime in read open requests, explaining that exclusive authority over atime or merging every read holder's times is needed to correctly delegate atime, which NFSD does not support. The author decided to grant OPEN_DELEGATE_READ instead, as it complies with RFC 9754 section 5.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about delegated timestamps being applied in the same nfsd_setattr() call as other attributes. They explained that this was causing problems, including EPERM for holders not owning the file and incorrect handling of ctime. The author proposed to decode time_deleg_access and time_deleg_modify into new fields in sa_iattr, apply the vetted times with notify_change(ATTR_FORCE) after nfsd_setattr() handles other attributes, and make changes to attrsset and nfsd4_secinfo_no_name_release().

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the NFS4ERR_DELAY error being reported when a GETATTR reply omits the SIZE attribute, which caused the waiter to mark the file as modified and report an incorrect size. The author added code to treat a reply without SIZE as failed in nfsd4_cb_getattr_done(), recalling the delegation instead.

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that a client can write to a file under a WRITE_ATTRS_DELEG delegation, return the delegation without updating the delegated timestamps, and then leave the file with its pre-delegation times after the filesystem is thawed. The reviewer questioned whether DELEGRETURN should wait for the filesystem to be thawed or if it's acceptable to return NFS4ERR_DELAY in this case.
reviews.raw_body:
DELEGRETURN reaches this trylock too, through destroy_delegation().
FMODE_NOCMTIME is already clear by then, so nothing sets mtime and
ctime afterward. A client that writes under a WRITE_ATTRS_DELEG and
returns it without a SETATTR of the delegated times, while the
filesystem is frozen, leaves the file with its pre-delegation times
after the thaw.

The laundromat and shutdown can't wait, but DELEGRETURN runs in an
nfsd thread, and the WRITEs that dirtied the file already block in
file_start_write(). Can DELEGRETURN wait for the thaw as well, or
might it be OK to return NFS4ERR_DELAY in this case?


--
Chuck Lever

2026-11-23.patch_summary: This patch fixes issues related to delegated timestamps in the NFSv4 protocol. Specifically, it addresses a problem where nfsd_setattr() waits for a delegation return while still holding the inode lock, which can cause the operation to time out and fail. The patch drops the inode lock during the wait period, allowing the file system to change while waiting for the delegation return. If the wait times out, the patch retries once before returning an error. This fix ensures that NFSv4 operations involving delegated timestamps are handled correctly and do not result in failed operations due to timing issues.
